judgment_text:
The Judgment of the Court was delivered by

Dr G. Jayachandran, J.:— This Tax Case appeal is filed by the Department, being aggrieved by the order of income tax Appellate Tribunal, Chennai ‘B’ Bench, Chennai, dated 8-10-2013, reversing the order of the revisional authority and confirming the order of the assessing authority.

2. In this case, under Section 263 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, the Commissioner of income tax-II at Coimbatore had considered the returns of the respondent and assessed Rs 1.30 crores as additional income in consequence to the survey carried out under Section 133A of the Income Tax Act, 1961. The assessee paid tax on the additional income. However, the Department had gone on revision and the revisional authority remanded the matter back to the assessing authority to redo the assessment, against which the assessee approached the income tax Appellate Tribunal. On considering the facts, the Tribunal had taken note of telescoping of the cash in hand to the income disclosed from the real estate business and taken it as a possible view to hold in favour of the assessee. As a result, the Tribunal set aside the order of the revisional authority.

3. Being aggrieved, the Department is before us.

4. The learned Senior Standing Counsel, appearing for the appellant Department, would submit that since the assessment was done under Section 263 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, pursuant to the survey carried out under Section 133A of the Act, the reasoning given by the assessing authority as well as the Tribunal for telescoping the undisclosed income was improper and the view expressed by the assessing authority, as confirmed by the Tribunal as a possible view, was incorrect.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent assessee has submitted that telescoping the cash in hand to the income explained is permissible under law and further the disputed tax liability falls within the threshold of Circular No. 09 of 2024 of Central Board of Direct Taxes, New Delhi, dated 17-9-2024, therefore, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

6. In this regard, learned Senior Standing Counsel, appearing for the Department, would submit that exemption in Circular No. 09 of 2024, dated 17-9-2024, which has modified the earlier Circular No. 05 of 2024, dated 15-3-2024, shall be subject to the condition stated in para 3.1 of the earlier Circular No. 05 of 2024. According to the learned Senior Standing Counsel, when the tax effect is not quantifiable or not involved, such as the case of registration of trusts or institutions under Sections 10 (23C), 12A/12AA/12AB of the Act, order passed under Section 263 of the Act, etc. the withdrawal circular has no application.

7. In response to the said submission, learned counsel for the respondent relied on two decisions, one by a Division Bench of this Court in Commissioner of income tax, Chennai v. The Willingdon Charitable Trust; by a Division Bench of Bombay High Court in principal Commissioner of income tax v. Jayesh V. Sheth. Both the above decisions indicate that non-application of Circular Nos. 05 of 2024 and 09 of 2024 is only in respect of cases, where tax liability is not quantified, and, even if assessment is made invoking Section 263 of the Income Tax Act, the above Circulars are applicable.

8. Further, the learned Senior Standing Counsel for the Department submitted that pending orders by the Tribunal, pursuant to the order passed by the revisional authority, the Assessing Officer has redone the assessment and imposed tax of Rs 1,26,03,870 by passing asessment order on 21-10-2013. It also appears that the assessee preferred an appeal against the said assessment order, but withdrew the same, in view of the order passed by the Tribunal. In any event, the fact remains that the earlier assessment having held to be right by the Tribunal, the second assessment by the Assessing Officer is superseded, in view of the order passed by the Tribunal.

9. Given the above circumstances and in view of the ratio laid down in the above said decisions, without adverting to the merits of the case and the substantial questions of law raised by the Department, we hold that the benefit of Circular Nos. 05 of 2024 and 09 of 2024 is to be extended to the respondent assessee herein, as the disputed tax amount is below the threshold of Rs 2.00 crores.

10. Tax Case appeal stands dismissed accordingly.
